raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I do not throw money around, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard. If yield drops, that hurts more than wasting a little input. I usually start from what worked for me last year and then adjust a bit by crop. Around Quzhou, wheat and maize are steady crops, and with my well water I can keep them from suffering badly if the weather turns dry. Cotton gives me a chance at better cash, so I will still keep some land in cotton, but I will not put all 5 mu into it because labor is tighter now and some people in the house work off-farm. For seed, I will use better seed where I have seen neighbors get a clean stand and decent yield. For wheat I will feed it enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, keep phosphorus under it, and give one light potash dressing because land here gets tired if I only chase nitrogen. For maize I will stay with hybrid seed, enough base fertilizer plus a topdress around the big flare stage, and 2 irrigations if rainfall is not enough. For cotton I will not be stingy with fertilizer because weak cotton never catches up well. I will use improved seed, give more potash than wheat and maize, water it about 3 times through the season, and spray more often because insects and disease can eat profit fast. Tillage-wise, I will plough before wheat and cotton where needed, and maize I can do with rotary tillage after wheat to save labor and time.
